narrative:
The model estimates a 62% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Most influential was that you have received other job opportunities while at your company. Having external offers strongly signals higher risk of departure compared to the majority of employees who stayed (77% of whom reported no such opportunities). This factor pushed the prediction noticeably toward leaving.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years also played a major role, though in the opposite direction. Most employees predicted to stay also had limited experience (50% in the 1-5 year range), so this characteristic actually pulled the prediction slightly toward staying. However, its effect was not strong enough to outweigh the other signals.

The third important factor was your employment in the "other" sector. This category showed a clearer tendency toward leaving compared to the more stable medical and education sectors that dominate among employees predicted to stay.

Taken together, the combination of external opportunities and sector-specific patterns created enough concern about potential departure to deny the promotion. Your organization should discuss retention strategies with you, particularly around career growth and exploring whether internal opportunities can match what you have been offered elsewhere. You may want to reflect on what would make staying more attractive long-term. (248 words)
